source: island_render.py — realistic-style placed-geometry render, all open-world surface tiles. z=0..3 rendered from real placed geometry (183 chunks, native 0.585 m/px). Two loading/blur fixes applied before this became the live pyramid: a halo-margin on the ground-cover density blur so adjacent chunks agree at their shared edge, and a footprint-aware instance-loading halo so meshes far larger than the flat 50 m halo (e.g. an 856 m cliff mesh) aren't dropped near a chunk boundary. z=-1..-5 are regenerated by repeated box-filter downsampling of that same z=0..3 raster — kept over v4's landscape-only tiles at every level, since they carry real forest/rock colour as a genuine regional tint instead of v4's flat material bake. Verified before promotion: 328/329 real adjacent chunk-boundary pairs across the whole island match each chunk's own local pixel-noise floor (no seam); one isolated pair (chunk z0_3_-6 | z0_4_-6, several heavily overlapping SM_Big_Cliff_* instances) still shows a visible boundary at native 0.585 m/px — a residual z-buffer sensitivity among near-tied overlapping giant meshes, not a data-loading gap. Coverage checked against v4's own land footprint: every v4 z=1 tile with content has at least one corresponding v5 z=3 tile (zero gaps); v5's own z=1 has more tiles than v4's (654 vs 650); every apparent 'interior hole' at z=3 (13 candidates) is a real water body, confirmed transparent in v4 at the same location too.
projection: SARDUCAA_MAP.world applied directly: lng = 0.213641 * worldX + 1783.4447, lat = 1709.1136 - 0.213641 * worldY. No art, no fitted registration.
note: Live pyramid as of 2026-08-22, replacing v4's landscape-only bake as the default map. Promoted from the staged 'v5props' directory (renamed to v5) after the verification above. v4/ is kept on disk unmodified as the rollback path; it is no longer referenced by registry.js.
